There's probably still quite a bit of reddit shell-shock here. So for a while, every time a pun is posted, there's likely to be a number of people thinking, 'Here we go again! Already turning into reddit.'

The issue with puns on reddit is that they clearly were the prime motivation for a large number of users. An inordinate number of submissions with interesting content would have a pun comment chain as the top post. And when you're just looking for interesting point and counterpoint on a topic, and yet again you have to scroll down pages of pun chains, it just gets tiring. It's not that people don't want to laugh, it's just the timing and placement. It's possible to both contribute to conversation and to be funny/entertaining.

I think wordplay and puns are kind of selfish on their own, in that they don't contribute to the conversation. So they're always a 'look how clever I am' kind of joke. And that 'look at me' attitude found all across reddit was what wore down at least a few defectors, myself included.

So yeah, funny is great. Everybody likes funny. But first make a relevant comment about Rand Paul's international policy. Then end with a fart joke or a pie in the face. Physical comedy is grossly underrepresented in message boards.

That's why whenever I have a pun, I try to add something meaningful to the discussion and then put the pun after my point. That way I get to make people laugh and add to the discussion.
